question: When a deal closes, can the company deliver it — build the deliverable, prove it, hand it over, record it, and add it to the library of proven goods — with the AI doing the work and Simon asked only for the hand-over, and with nothing unproven ever handed over or added?
why: Simon's AI-first company spec (2026-10-28), build step 5: 'the operations loop (closed deal → delivered → recorded → library grows)'. The pattern library is the product; a delivery that grows it is the company's compounding move.

design.deliverable: A deliverable is a receipt card exactly like the voice's (repo, full commit, path, sha256, facts). The IO fetches the receipt from GitHub at its pin and hashes it; kar-voice's claim gate (vendored byte-identical) decides whether it is proven.
design.ops: src/ops.mjs deliver(deal, { card, gate, approve, library }): 'build' (put to the conductor in its own words: internal work) → the deliverable and its gate result → if the gate refuses: stop, nothing handed over, nothing added → 'hand the deliverable to @<handle>' put to the conductor (Simon's lane) → asked → handed over (a dry run) only on an approval of that exact text → a delivery record in the journal → the library gains one entry, never a duplicate.
design.record: The delivery record is an entry in the hash-chained journal (who, what, which receipt by pin and hash, when). It is not signed by a key in this step.
design.noSwitch: No kernel in this repo exports anything that turns a ledger on or attaches value to a record. A job that asks for it is Simon's (the conductor's ledger flag).

card.name: The liveware pilot
card.claim: its ingest gateway admitted 180,000 genuine records and refused 0 of them

card.name: A grown churn brain
card.claim: held-out AUC 0.796 on 720 rows it never saw

card.name: A grown churn brain
card.claim: held-out AUC 0.896 on 720 rows it never saw

library: The library starts as the voice's four genuine receipt cards that passed its gate (witness-ms, kar-controller, churn-book, conductor) plus credit-book: five entries.

claims.claim: D1 and D2 are each delivered exactly once: one build, one hand-over asked of Simon, one delivery record, and the library grows from 5 to 7.
D3, whose card moves a receipt number, is refused by the claim gate: nothing handed over, nothing recorded, nothing added.
claims.pass: refused; 0 hand-overs, 0 records, library unchanged by it

claims.claim: The hand-over waits for Simon: walked again with no approval, D1 is built and proven but never handed over, recorded or added.
No switch: no kernel exports a name that turns a ledger on, and the conductor sends 'switch on the ledger' to Simon flagged ledger.
claims.pass: 0 such exports; simon with flag ledger

claims.claim: Delivering D1 twice adds it to the library once.

scope: Two fixture deals delivered with real, pinned receipts from the estate's own repos as the deliverables; the hand-over is a dry run and the approvals are rehearsal records. What a real deliverable contains is agreed per deployment.
